key_insight: Using Chow forms, the paper improves complexity bounds from PSPACE to the counting hierarchy (CH) for several algebraic-geometry decision problems involving equidimensional components.
engineering_relevance: These results sharpen theoretical complexity guarantees for symbolic-computation tasks such as component membership and approximate polynomial satisfiability.
method: Represent equidimensional components of projective varieties using Chow forms.
Combine geometric resolutions with threshold circuits for multivariate resultants.
Construct polylogtime-uniform, constant-depth, exponential-size threshold circuits to compute the Chow forms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity results, including CH decision procedures and degree computation in FP^CH, rather than empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The exponential-size circuit construction does not by itself establish a practical or polynomial-time implementation.
paper_title: Some algebraic and geometric computations in CH via Chow forms
